references.text: Joel describes a locust plague that destroys trees and crops, which directly mirrors the curse in Deuteronomy that locusts will devour all fruit and every tree.
The Lord promises to replace what locusts and other insects have devoured, contrasting with the curse where insects destroy the harvest.
The locust plague in Egypt demonstrates God's judgment through insects consuming all vegetation, the same pattern warned against Israel in the curse of Deuteronomy.
Amos describes how God sent locusts that devoured gardens and vineyards, a fulfillment of the curse concerning insects destroying crops.
Solomon's prayer mentions locusts as a possible plague over the land, acknowledging the curse from Deuteronomy as a real threat.
